questions.stem: Which international watchdog body issues the 'Grey List' and 'Black List' to countries based on their compliance with anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism financing norms?

options.option_text: Financial Action Task Force (FATF)
Bank for International Settlements (BIS)
Interpol (International Criminal Police Organization)
International Monetary Fund — Article IV consultations

questions.explanation: FATF is the inter-governmental body that sets global standards for combating money laundering and terrorism financing; it places non-compliant countries on its 'Grey List' (increased monitoring) or 'Black List' (call for action). BIS handles central-bank cooperation, not AML monitoring. IMF Article IV consultations are macroeconomic surveillance, not a listing mechanism.

questions.stem: The principal judicial organ of the United Nations, the International Court of Justice (ICJ), is headquartered in which city?

options.option_text: Geneva, Switzerland (seat of UN Human Rights Council)
Vienna, Austria (seat of IAEA and UNODC headquarters)
The Hague, Netherlands (also home of the ICC)
Brussels, Belgium (seat of NATO and EU institutions)

questions.explanation: The ICJ, established in 1945 under the UN Charter, sits at the Peace Palace in The Hague. A common distractor is Geneva, which hosts many UN specialised agencies but not the ICJ. The ICC (International Criminal Court) is a separate body also in The Hague but is not a UN organ.

questions.stem: India and Pakistan were formally admitted as full members of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) at which summit and in which year?

options.option_text: 2015 — Ufa Summit held in Russia
2017 — Astana Summit held in Kazakhstan
2016 — Tashkent Summit held in Uzbekistan
2019 — Bishkek Summit held in Kyrgyzstan

questions.explanation: India and Pakistan were granted observer status in 2005 and formally inducted as full members at the Astana Summit in June 2017. The Ufa 2015 summit began their accession process (memoranda signed), but full membership was conferred only in 2017. Candidates often confuse the 2015 process-start with the 2017 completion.

questions.stem: Which major economy pulled out of the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP) negotiations in November 2019, citing inadequate safeguards against import surges and trade deficit concerns?

options.option_text: India, citing trade imbalance and weak rules-of-origin norms
Pakistan, due to ongoing geopolitical tensions with members
Bangladesh, to protect its domestic garment and textile sector
Sri Lanka, citing vulnerability of its agricultural sector

questions.explanation: India withdrew from RCEP at the ASEAN Summit in Bangkok (November 2019), concerned that its manufacturing and dairy sectors could be swamped by cheap Chinese and New Zealand imports; weak rules-of-origin could allow goods re-routed through ASEAN. Pakistan, Bangladesh, and Sri Lanka were never RCEP negotiating parties — only ASEAN-10 + China, Japan, South Korea, Australia, and New Zealand.

questions.stem: BIMSTEC (Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation) established its permanent secretariat in which city?

options.option_text: Colombo, Sri Lanka — host of the inaugural BIMSTEC summit
Dhaka, Bangladesh — home of the BIMSTEC Secretariat since 2014
Bangkok, Thailand — where BIMSTEC was originally founded in 1997
Kathmandu, Nepal — geographically central to all BIMSTEC members

questions.explanation: The BIMSTEC Secretariat was established in Dhaka, Bangladesh in 2014. BIMSTEC was indeed founded in Bangkok in 1997 (as BIST-EC), which is the most tempting distractor. The secretariat being in Dhaka is a separate fact from the founding location — examiners frequently test this distinction.

questions.stem: The Nagoya Protocol on Access and Benefit-Sharing — which governs how genetic resources and associated traditional knowledge may be accessed and how benefits are shared — is a supplementary agreement to which international convention?

options.option_text: UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)
Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD), adopted at COP-10 in 2010
Basel Convention on Control of Transboundary Hazardous Wastes
Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species (CITES)

questions.explanation: The Nagoya Protocol was adopted at CBD COP-10 in Nagoya, Japan in 2010, supplementing the CBD's third objective (fair benefit-sharing from genetic resources). CITES regulates trade in endangered species — a plausible wrong answer — but it has no protocol on genetic-resource access. The Basel Convention covers hazardous waste, not biodiversity.

questions.stem: Under the UN Charter, which article specifically empowers the Security Council to take military enforcement action — using air, sea, or land forces — when non-military coercive measures have been or are likely to be inadequate?

options.option_text: Article 39 of Chapter VII — determination of threats to peace
Article 41 of Chapter VII — non-military enforcement measures
Article 51 of Chapter VII — inherent right of individual self-defence
Article 42 of Chapter VII — military action by air, sea, or land forces

questions.explanation: Article 42 (Chapter VII) authorises the UNSC to take military action when Article 41 (sanctions and non-military measures) are deemed inadequate. Article 39 is the gateway clause — it empowers the UNSC to 'determine' a threat — but confers no enforcement power itself. Article 51 is the separate right of self-defence available to member states, not a UNSC enforcement provision.
